_comment: Light Path Simulator, drawn by emtk.view_form over LightPathPanel (gui/panel.py). The graph itself, the connection form and the Easy Mode setup are drawn by gui/app.py (a canvas and a shared widget a spec cannot express).

sections.description: Save and load the optical graph, keep it as a preset for Easy Mode, store the simulation in MMFDB, export the instrument setting, open the guide or the help.

buttons.label: Save Graph
buttons.description: Save the current graph (nodes, connections, component choices and layout) to a JSON file.

buttons.label: Load Graph
buttons.description: Load a graph, or an Easy Mode preset, from a JSON file. You can also drop the file on the window.

buttons.label: Save Preset
buttons.description: Save the current graph under a name as an optical path preset for Easy Mode.

buttons.label: Save to MMFDB
buttons.description: Persist the current graph and its simulation in MMFDB under a name you give.

buttons.label: Load from MMFDB
buttons.description: Choose a previously saved simulation from MMFDB and load its graph.

buttons.label: Export
buttons.description: Export the simulated instrument setting as a JSON file. Greyed until a simulation has been calculated.

buttons.label: Guide
buttons.description: A step-by-step walk through the tool.

buttons.label: Help
buttons.description: The help page: components, simulation, results and files.

sections.description: Add the selected component to the middle of the visible graph, or restore the standard two-colour path.

buttons.label: Add to Graph
buttons.description: Add the component selected in the list above to the middle of the graph. Double-clicking a row does the same.

buttons.label: Reset to Default
buttons.description: Restore the standard path: two lasers, a sample, a dichroic splitter, two filters and two detectors. Replaces the graph.

sections.description: The optical components you can add to the graph. Select one and press Add to Graph, or double-click it.
Arrange the nodes by signal flow, frame the whole graph, or remove the selected nodes and links.

buttons.label: Arrange
buttons.description: Lay out the nodes by optical signal flow and frame the complete graph.

buttons.label: Fit
buttons.description: Frame the entire beam path without changing the saved node positions.

buttons.label: Delete Selected
buttons.description: Delete the selected nodes and connections. Greyed while nothing is selected.

sections.label: Show minimap
sections.description: Show a small overview of the graph for navigating a large optical network.
Backend options.

items.label: Use configured RPC server
items.description: Use the existing ChiSurf/MMFDB connection and session token instead of the local scientific backend.

items.label: Auto update
items.description: Queue one fresh simulation after every edit of the graph or the Easy Mode setup.

sections.label: Spectra database
sections.description: Path of the MMFDB spectra database; empty uses the configured database.
Reload the catalogue of dye, transmission and detector spectra from the selected backend.

buttons.label: Load Catalogue
buttons.description: Load the dye, transmission and detector spectra from the selected backend.

sections.label: Name
sections.description: Name stored with the simulation and its MMFDB artifacts when you press Save to MMFDB.
Run the simulation of the current graph; stop a running backend call.

buttons.label: Calculate Emission Intensity
buttons.description: Propagate the spectra through the graph and fill the detector signals, the excitation, emission and detected crosstalk matrices and the Förster radii.

buttons.label: Stop
buttons.description: Discard the pending simulation when its backend call finishes; an MMFDB save completes consistently.

sections.description: Simulations stored in MMFDB. Select one and press Load.

columns.title: Name
columns.description: The name the simulation was saved under.

sections.description: Detected intensity per laser line, detector and dye.

columns.title: Detected Intensity
columns.description: Detected intensity of this dye in this channel for this laser line.

sections.description: Excitation probability: laser line (rows) by dye (columns).
Emission probability: dye (rows) by detector channel (columns).
Detected crosstalk: laser line and dye (rows) by detector channel (columns).
Förster radius of each donor and acceptor pair, from the simulated spectra.

sections.label: From
sections.description: The node producing the optical spectrum or scalar parameter.

sections.label: Out port
sections.description: Zero-based output-port index on the source node.

sections.label: To
sections.description: The node that consumes the selected source output.

sections.label: In port
sections.description: Zero-based input-port index on the target node.
Create the connection described above, or remove the selected one.

buttons.label: Connect Ports
buttons.description: Create an optical connection from the chosen output port to the chosen input port; one source may feed each input.

buttons.label: Remove Link
buttons.description: Remove the link selected in the list below. Greyed while none is selected. The Delete key does the same.

sections.description: The optical links of the graph. Select one to remove it.

columns.title: From
columns.description: The node and output port the link starts at.

columns.title: To
columns.description: The node and input port the link ends at.
